Blockchain (BC) technology, mainly invented with the cryptocurrency Bitcoin, can bring these features. This paper presents an in-depth investigation of how to tweak blockchain to meet the unique requirements of the IoT to produce Blockchain-based IoT (BIoT) applications. The authors also provide a brief overview of the current IoT authentication mechanisms for safe data transfer and provide an in-depth scrutiny of the previous research.

articleTitle: Optimizing Device Selection in the Healthcare Sector: A Comparative Study of AHP and ELECTRE Methods for Informed Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Multi-criteria decision-making, MCDM consists of many methods to assist the decision-maker in selecting the best alternatives. MCDM has seen its application in a huge variety of problem domains and the healthcare sector is no exception. Medical domain is more challenging as it involves uncertainties, conflicting requirements, judgments from more than one decision maker and a mix of qualitative and quantitative data. The healthcare sector hugely depends upon various imaging techniques for the diagnosis of disease. In the past few decades, ultrasound techniques emerged as the most popular and effective aid in disease diagnosis. Thus for good and cost-effective diagnostics, medical experts should be equipped with good ultrasound machines. Selecting a good ultrasound machine needs evaluation of many features, thus MCDM methods can be deployed. The present paper proposes a comparative the study of most popular MCDM method, AHP and not so not-so-popular Electre method in the medical device selection in healthcare sector. The present study is considering Six Criteria and five alternatives, that can be scaled up to include more criteria and alternatives.

articleTitle: Neural Networking for Human Neuroplasticity With Deep Neural Network for Finding Human Talent
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: A key component of understanding the human brain's information processing mechanism is neural networking, which seeks to create a quantifiable connection between the stimuli and the triggered brain processes. Population receptive field (pRF) models have gained a lot of traction and demonstrated steady advancement in the field of visual neuroscience recently. These models can describe the functioning of neurons in basic neuroplasticity. However, the expressiveness and interpretability of previous models are significantly constrained by their reliance on either imprecise parameter estimation methods or tight prior beliefs regarding pRF. In this study, we present a unique neural networking architecture that trains deep neural networks to recognize “where” and “what.” Two separate elements that are involved in neuroplasticity are the spatial feature (“where”) and feature selection (“what”) of neuron clusters. The method described involves three main steps. The initial phase is utilizing a pretrained deep neural network (DNN) to encode visual data into preliminary features. To find “where,” these features are further refined through the use of channel attention and spatial receptive field. In order to determine “what,” the improved features are then simultaneously regressed onto voxel activity. This modeling approach incorporates smoothness and sparsity regularizations, enabling us to automatically determine the essential receptive field size without assuming any specific shape in advance. Using multi-voxel joint networking models, the study investigates extending voxel-wise modeling to successfully improve the accuracy of underperforming voxels. The research demonstrates that this approach, which involves fewer prior constraints but achieves better networking performance, offers an effective way to design neural networks for studying human neuroplasticity.

articleTitle: Human Factors in Cybersecurity Awareness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Human behavior is both a factor in the emergence of cyber threats and a means of protecting against them. This study provides a thorough analysis of human aspects related to cybersecurity awareness. Cybersecurity is very dependent on humans who are still the weakest link despite the advancement in technology. The psychological, behavioral, and sociocultural aspects of cybersecurity are the focus of this study. The main concern is how these elements affect security, and how people perceive risks and implement security measures. This paper analyzes the pros and cons of cybersecurity awareness programs, their engagement, and financial constraints, and uses case studies to demonstrate how ignoring human aspects can impact real-world outcomes. The paper suggests a middle way that embraces both technology and human supervision and explores the connection between technological advances and human behavior. In the end, it finishes with some recommendations for enhancing cybersecurity awareness by pointing out policy implications, educating particular audiences, and sharing good practices. For successful combating of cyber threats, the study emphasizes the need for an integrated strategy that synchronizes human actions, corporate values, technological innovations, and legislative systems.

Author Keywords: Sociocultural Influences on Cybersecurity and Cybersecurity Training Programs

articleTitle: Distinguishing Truth from Deception: Employing Machine Learning for Rumor Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: One of the most significant problems in the Internet and social media world we live in today is fake news. The fact that news can travel great distances in a matter of hours is a blessing, but it is also upsetting to witness several individuals and organizations disseminating false information. Many false news reports feature propaganda against an individual, group, organization, or political party. There are too many phoney news stories for one human to handle. Therefore, it is necessary to have machine learning classifiers that can recognize these bogus news reports automatically. In this study data of fake news collected from kaggle and different approaches applied into it like Logistic regression, hard voting classifier, graded boosting, adaboost and random forest approach. This will help any one to make right decision and analyze the truthiness involved into the news. Applying such algorithms techniques will make the environment peaceful and also help to reduce riots among different religions or communities, which is very often in many countries. These techniques will also be helpful in making the readers or viewers smart by simply not relying on any news blindly but also to use smart techniques by which they can able to decide about the percentage of truthiness in any news on social media platform.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach With PSO for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: With the advent of internet and emergence of a digital landscape in the present world, sharing information online is prevalent. While this has made life much easier by facilitating speedy responses and widespread connectivity, it comes with its own set of challenges, the most concerning being threats to network security. The incessant threats to confidentiality of the information calls for measures to protect sensitive data. Network Intrusion Detection Systems have proved to be fruitful in monitoring malicious activities and thereby ensuring security of data by preventing unauthorized access in the systems. In this study, multiple machine learning classifiers were utilized to analyze the NSL-KDD dataset for network intrusions. DoS and Probe subsets were used and attempts were made to boost the performance of the machine learning models. Addressing class imbalance problem with the aid of SMOTE was crucial in stimulating unbiased model training. Machine learning algorithms like Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, XG Boost and Decision Trees were employed to train the models. The accuracies of the models were compared before and after implementing Particle Swarm Optimization for hyperparameter tuning.

articleTitle: Designing an Intelligent Data Transmission Strategy Between Entities Using Wireless Communication Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Data security is of the utmost importance in wireless sensor networks due to the massive amounts of data collected and sent between nodes. An improved security method for wireless sensor networks is presented in this paper. This mechanism takes into account the application, the security level, and the bit error rate simultaneously. In order to provide the user with the ability to select between unsecure and secure modes, we made use of reserved bits of the frame control field that are contained within the communication header. The Secured and Intelligent Data Transmission Protocol (SIDTP) is the name of the unified perceptual information transmission model that is established in this research. Its purpose is to compensate for the unequal distribution of cognitive radio users across different wireless LANs. For the purpose of determining whether or not the suggested scheme is effective, the proposed model will be cross-validated with the traditional data transmission model known as Wireless Data Transmission Protocol (WDTP). The approach has the potential to optimize the utilization of spectrum resources in an efficient manner. In addition, to help lessen the risks connected with wireless networks, this study lays out a technique for transmitting data using cyclic delay full diversity sensing information coding. In order to evaluate the performance of the system against a variety of correlation coefficients, we developed a system simulation model. The result of the study showed that cyclic delay diversity systems had overall interference intensity similar to frequency division duplex as well as time division duplex. As an added bonus, this enhances its anti-jamming attack capabilities. The proposed system has been planned and implemented, and significant trials have been carried out in an industrial setting. Additionally, a prototype of the system has been designed. Compared to conventional communication interfaces that are only equipped with a single wireless interface, the results demonstrate that the system that has been presented is capable of achieving much higher levels of network reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Navigating the Skies: A Comprehensive Analysis of Airport Automation and Its Impact on Passenger Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Airport automation and digitization are now essential in light of the difficulties facing the travel sector. The travel industry is remarkably flexible, even in light of recent setbacks, as demonstrated by the ongoing digital revolution. This endeavor is motivated by the realization that shorter wait times and more efficient identity verification procedures translate into a traveler's overall experience being much better. The primary focus of this study is the coordination of systems that manage travelers' identities, which calls for smooth cooperation between government border agencies, airlines, and airports. Ensuring a truly frictionless passenger journey requires the integration of multiple touchpoints, from check-in to boarding. The objectives of this automation investment are to maximize resource allocation, improve overall customer experience, and accelerate passenger flow.

articleTitle: DERM-AI: A Convolutional Neural Network Based Approach For Skin Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: This paper shows how convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are useful for accurately and quickly diagnosing skin issues, underscoring the need of utilizing state-of-the-art machine learning approaches for accurate and fast diagnosis. A CNN architecture including convolutional and pooling layers, fully linked layers, and a softmax classifier was developed to handle the problem of diagnosing skin diseases. The CNN model was trained using stochastic gradient descent, and its hyperparameters were adjusted using grid search and random search. Future research in this area may benefit from the insights the study offers on CNN model construction and application for skin disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Exploring ML Methods for Sentiment Analysis in Text Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Data Analysis has become an important part of our life, as it helps us to draw useful information, decision-making conclusions on any particular raw data. One component of digital data analysis is sentiment analysis. Sentiment analysis evaluates the emotional tone of textual data and classifies it as neutral, negative, or positive. In business, this analysis is frequently utilized for market social media monitoring, market research, consumer feedback and many more. In order to automate the procedure, machine learning models that recognize patterns in labeled data are frequently used. The objective is to derive meaningful insights from textual data so that decisions can be made with knowledge, effectively. In order to provide important insights into public opinion and behavior, this study uses machine learning techniques to investigate the sentiments conveyed in Twitter data. A wide range of Twitter posts, including ones about trending hashtags, events, and subjects, are gathered as part of the process. Sentiment analysis is done using machine learning algorithms. Sentiment analysis and examples of human language are used to train machine learning models. Following this training, machine learning is used by sentiment analysis software to evaluate and rank human language according to its previous training. The current study proposes a technique that best analyzes the sentiments of the text used in social media is gradient boosting classifier. With this method, an additive model can be built in a step-by-step, forward fashion and any differentiable loss function can be optimized. There are n-class regression trees that are fitted on the negative gradient of the loss function, which could be the multiclass log loss or the binary loss. This process is repeated in each step. In the particular case of binary classification, just one regression tree is induced. The computational results demonstrates that gradient boosting approach with an accuracy of 93.62% which outperforms is preferable to other classifiers.

articleTitle: Mitigating E-Commerce Security Risks with Blockchain: A Multi-Layered Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The look explores the mixing of blockchain into e-commerce structures by using focused on the demanding situations. Our proposed multi-degree framework enhances records protection, scalability and stakeholder communication at the same time as considering ethical implications. In particular, with the aid of using zero-know-how proofs (ZKPs), isotropic encryption, and smart settlement control, we make sure strong security and privacy. The technique includes a systematic literature evaluate, conceptual framework improvement, and iterations, which provide precious insights for destiny research Our architecture gives a systematic technique to overcoming obstacles to adoption blockchain tech in e-trade so, sell agree with and operational efficiency. By combining the decentralized nature of blockchain with new technology, we lay the inspiration for steady and transparent e-commerce transactions. This paper contributes to improving the use of blockchain in e-commerce by way of offering a comprehensive analysis and sensible framework. With readability and specificity, we goal to improve security and productivity within the eCommerce environment.

articleTitle: Receiver Efficient Location-Based Service Scheme by OT Using PKE
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The widespread adoption of mobile devices with location capabilities has increased the demand for Location Based Services (LBS). In the LBS scheme, the vehicle users submit their query to the LBS server, which in return responds to the requested query. However, conventional LBS schemes pose threats to both the vehicle users' and the LBS servers' data privacy. Existing solutions, such as k-anonymity, Dummy sequence and Caching schemes overlook the critical aspect of the data privacy of the LBS server and the computational constraints of vehicle users. Here, we propose a receiver-efficient scheme using Oblivious Transfer (OT) with ElGamal with an Elliptic Curve Cryptosystem (ECC). Our scheme aims to safeguard the query and location privacy of vehicle users, and the LBS servers' data privacy, while also maintaining constant-time computations at the receivers' end.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Image Synthesis: Using Stack GAN to Enhance Cybersecurity Application of Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Text-to-image synthesis, a transformative application of artificial intelligence, converts textual descriptions into vivid images, with implications ranging from artistic expression to cybersecurity. This paper explores Stack Generative Adversarial Networks (Stack GAN) as an architectural innovation, enhancing image quality in two stages: Stage I and Stage II, each employing generators and discriminators to produce high-resolution images. With a focus on data integrity and system security, encryption algorithms safeguard sensitive input data. The Stack GAN model, coupled with conditional augmentation, improves resource efficiency, and content linkage, and mitigates over-fitting. Results demonstrate the model's robustness, offering utility in information and network security through enhanced fraud detection, user authentication, and visualization of security policies. This research underscores the fusion of AI's creative capabilities with traditional and innovative security measures.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ensemble Machine Learning Models for Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Recent developments in electronic payment and e-commerce have led to a rise in digital fraud cases, including credit card fraud. Within the financial services industry, identifying credit card fraud is still a difficult task that can have significant effects on consumers' and financial institutions' reputations. Therefore, it is crucial to implement systems capable of detecting credit card fraud. This research utilizes the European Cardholder Data Collection to assess the efficacy of ensemble machine learning techniques in identifying credit card fraud. The European cardholder data set is subjected to a rigorous assessment and evaluation of series of machine learning models, such as Gradient Boosting, Random Forest and CAT Boost, to detect fraudulent transactions. It has been noted that the dataset is unbalanced, which may indicate that the models' performance is not very ideal. The study suggests using data sampling strategies to achieve a balanced distribution of data across various algorithms that yield optimal outcomes. The main goal is to identify the model that performs best for machine learning classification problems by comparing the performance of different models. The results of this study will support further initiatives to improve credit card transaction security and lower financial losses brought on by fraud.

articleTitle: AI Fitness Trainer: Dynamic Motion Correction and Real-Time Feedback for Enhancing Self-Managed Workouts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: With the COVID-19 pandemic making self-managed exercise ever more popular, this project aims to create a reliable motion correction model through machine learning methods. The study tackles the urgent need for safe and efficient workout rou-tines that don't require medical supervision. The research process consists of three main stages: the model is integrated into a real-time 3D human position estimator for instant feedback during workouts; a graph convolutional network (GCN) architecture with dynamic temporal warping loss is implemented to align and optimize 3D posture sequences; and exercise videos, 2D/3D position data, and accuracy labels are carefully collected as the dataset. The results point to a significant improvement in exercise efficacy and safety, which may lower the risk of injury and boost workout results. In addition, the project promotes independence from professional supervision by following the trend toward independent exercise. The ramifications go beyond fitness and promise revolutionary changes in a variety of fields, including physical therapy, sports performance enhancement, healthcare monitoring, and rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Contrast and Colour Improvement based Haze Removal of Satellite Images using Fusion Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Satellite imagery plays a pivotal role in various domains, yet its utility can be hindered by atmospheric haze, leading to degraded contrast and color fidelity. This paper presents a pioneering methodology aimed at ameliorating these issues through a Fusion Technique. Leveraging Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and Unsharp Mask Filtering, our approach systematically processes Hazy Satellite Images to generate Contrast Enhanced Outputs, White Balanced Outputs, Chromatic Weight Maps, Saliency Weight Maps, and Luminance Weight Maps. Subsequently, a fusion mechanism amalgamates these components, yielding a Dehazed Image of enhanced quality. Evaluation metrics including Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Entropy, and absolute mean brightness error (AMBE) attest to the superior performance of our method. By addressing the challenges inherent in haze removal from satellite imagery, our approach not only enhances visual appeal but also enriches the informational content of the scenes captured, thus fostering advancements in satellite image processing and analysis.

articleTitle: Feature Selection in Intrusion Detection using Jaccard's Needham Similarity Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The Intrusion Detection System (IDS) plays a vital role in upholding network security, safeguarding network resources and infrastructures. This paper presents an in-depth methodology for enhancing intrusion detection using machine learning in the context of network security. The study integrates various techniques to measure classification performance, with focus on a unique feature selection algorithm called Jaccard-Needham similarity algorithm. This innovative approach quanti-fies dissimilarity between features, strategically deselecting those with the least similarity, thereby enhancing the model's discriminative power. The culmination of our research entails a thorough comparative analysis of machine learning methodologies, encompassing Decision Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost, Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), and Logistic Regression. The evaluation process is conducted using the Jaccards feature selection algorithm across different thresholds and is also compared with other existing feature selection techniques. The analysis reveals compelling results with our proposed approach giving highest accuracy (99.41%) at 0.0001 threshold for Jaccard index with top 15 features, outperforming the other evaluated feature selection techniques. This outcome underscores its effectiveness in identifying and selecting features conducive to superior model performance.

articleTitle: Unifying Traditional and Machine Learning Approaches for Robust Malware Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The pervasive nature of cybersecurity threats necessitates innovative approaches to bolster defense mechanisms. This research introduces a dynamic and adaptive framework for malware classification, integrating advanced machine learning algorithms with real-time scanning capabilities. The proposed system goes beyond traditional signature-based methods, offering a robust solution to identify and classify malicious files in real-time. We present a detailed analysis of the framework's methodology, encompassing diverse dataset collection, model development, and seamless integration into a user-friendly application. Through rigorous testing and evaluation, our framework demonstrates superior accuracy, precision, and responsiveness, showcasing its effectiveness in the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity. User feedback mechanisms and continuous model training further enhance the framework's adaptability to emerging threats. This research contributes a comprehensive solution to address the pressing challenges of malware detection, providing a valuable tool for cybersecurity professionals and organizations striving to fortify their defenses against evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: Canine Guard: A Novel Canine Repellent System Using Ultrasonic Wave Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Our prototype is to designed two-wheeler safety device, which repel stray animals, like dogs, from chasing vehicles. We developed a device which aimed to aiding the protection for the riders from stray dogs they might encounter during biking or motorcycle rides in cities or rural areas. We investigated how dogs behave and what riders desire in such a device. Our repellent uses sounds that dogs dislike to keep them away from bicycles and motorcycles. Individuals who trailed it stated they felt more secure and confident while traveling in areas where there is a high dog population. We're still in the process of enhancing it to be more efficacious from greater distances, last for a longer duration, and function in various scenarios.

articleTitle: Human Detection to Mitigate Excessive Electrical Energy Usage in Communal Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the issue of increased electrical energy consumption in communal settings, with a specific focus on areas such as restrooms and multiplexes as the primary areas of investigation. Not only does the observed behavior increase the financial requirements of end-users and facility operators, but it also places a major strain on energy grids, which in turn leads to a rise in carbon emissions and an intensification of environmental concerns. A unique approach that makes use of the TensorFlow Object Counting API is proposed by the current inquiry as a means of addressing the concern that was highlighted earlier. The purpose of this strategy is to develop a system that can precisely count human subjects in real-time when they are present. To effectively decerase the amount of electricity that is not required, the primary objective of this cutting-edge system is to precisely identify and count the number of people that are present in shared spaces. When it comes to the development of advanced object counting systems, the open-source framework that has been developed on the TensorFlow is a platform that offers a method that is both user-friendly and efficient. Within the realms of item identification, tracking, and counting, the system exhibits capabilities that are both spectacular and resilient. By addressing the dual problems of rising electricity bills and negative effects on the environment, this technology offers a potential solution to the problem. Through this study, an attempt is made to investigate the factors that lead to excessive energy use and to propose a practical solution to this sianificant problem.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain-enabled Secure Birth Certificate Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: With the recent advancement in technology, forgery activities have become more sophisticated and challenging to detect. This necessitates the development of advanced technologies that can counteract the illicit practices over digital platforms to streamline their operation. This article confronts the birth certificate forgery activities to strengthen the document verification system. In that context, we proposed an artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain-based reliable framework for securing an individual's birth records. For that, we utilized a standard birth record dataset comprised of tampered and non-tampered data, which is trained on different machine learning (ML) algorithms, such as K-nearest neighbours (KNN), decision tree (DT), logistic regression (LR), and perceptron (PT) for binary classification tasks. Further, the predicted data from the AI models are forwarded to the blockchain network for secure data storage. In that context, we first designed a smart contract that validates the legitimacy of the predicted data; upon validation, it is forwarded to the interplanetary file system (IPFS) for hash computation. Integrating IPFS improves the scalability and response time of the blockchain network. Lastly, the proposed work is evaluated by considering different evaluation metrics, such as training accuracy, statistics measures (precision, recall, and F1 score), blockchain transaction and execution cost. Integrating blockchain and AI addresses data security, confidentiality, and accuracy in birth registration, providing a robust solution against potential digital and offline threats.

articleTitle: Medicinal Plant Classification Using Transfer Learning Through Hybrid Machine Learning and Image Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Medicinal plants play a crucial role in traditional medicine and healthcare systems worldwide. In this study, we proposed a comprehensive approach for the detection of medicinal plants using a combination of DL features extracted from VGG16 architecture, along with traditional methods encompassing shape, texture, statistical, and color features. Initially, we loaded a dataset of medicinal plant images from Kaggle, providing a diverse and representative collection of species. Next, features from VGG16 extracted for producing a feature vector. Additionally, we augmented these features with traditional methods to create final feature vector. Subsequently, ML models, including SVM, Random Forests, Decision Trees, logistic regression and KNN applied to final dataset to classify medicinal plant species. Through comparative analysis, it is identified the best-performing model as random forest with 98.3% accuracy and 98% of f1 score for medicinal plant classification. The findings shed light on the effectiveness of combining deep learning and traditional feature extraction methods for accurate and reliable medicinal plant detection, offering insights into potential applications in botanical research and healthcare.

articleTitle: Implementation of Cryptographic Algorithm for Cloud Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Cloud computing has a wide variety of applications, one of which is the storage of substantial amounts of data on remote servers. Numerous businesses take use of this feature, which is known as “cloud storage.” Therefore, it may be necessary to archive the information, which may come in the form of text, audio, video, and many othermedia. on an effort to keep sensitive data safe on the cloud, researchers have built a number of unique algorithms that draw on a wide range of methods. As a result, a thorough examination of the related literature has beenconducted. In an effort to ensure the safety of statistical data, this research will make anattempt to highlight key algorithms. This study intends to make such attempt.

articleTitle: Efficient Token Transfer Using ERC-20 Decentralized Exchange
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The implementation of blockchain-based token transfers has emerged as a transformative tool for innovation and enhanced financial inclusion. To implement Blockchain based token transfers, smart contracts play a pivotal role in automating complex processes, enhancing efficiency, and driving innovation for tokenized assets and decentralized applications (dApps) that can be run on Ethereum. With rising popularity of smart contracts in 2015, necessity for a standardized token approach within the Ethereum ecosystem is recognized. To address interoperability issues and challenges in exchanging tokens between different applications, the Ethereum Request for Commet-20 (ERC20) standard was introduced through the Ethereum Request for Comment (ERC) process. Since then, several numerous schemes have been proposed efforts to enhance token transfers and implementations while adhering to ERC-20 standards. Despite the substantial progress made in optimizing the functionality and efficiency of token transfers, achieving a truly user-friendly experience has remained an ongoing challenge. To address this challenge, several schemes have been proposed to refine the user interface and experience associated with ERC-20 token transfers. Our research work proposes a practical approach to address concerns by creating a simple user-friendly decentralized web application (Web3) using smart contracts that adhere to ERC-20 standards. By focusing on the development of a seamless user experience, the system developed aims to empower users to send tokens effortlessly by connecting to various wallets available in the market.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning and Blockchain for Enhanced Transparency and Traceability in the Indian Herbal Product Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Medicinal plants have been a cornerstone of healthcare practices globally, serving a significant population in developing countries who rely on affordable herbal remedies. However, the current marketing system through Mandis and wholesale markets suffers from opacity. Numerous intermediaries create an information gap for farmers regarding fair pricing and market trends. Additionally, concerns exist about misidentification and adulteration of medicinal plants due to limited knowledge among collectors and traders. The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB) recognizes the need for a robust supply chain. This paper proposes a blockchain-based platform ‘Indian Herbal Blockchain Network (IHBN)’ integrated with Deep Learning for image processing. The deep learning model has achieved a decent accuracy of 90.24% which decreases the chance of misidentification. The platform ensures transparent traceability of medicinal plants from source to consumer, along with accurate identification using image analysis. This system promotes transparency within the medicinal plant supply chain, reducing the risk of adulteration and improving overall trust.

articleTitle: Exploring Deepfake Detection: A Comparative Study of CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning methodologies has given rise to worries regarding the misuse of hyper-realistic multimedia due to the introduction of deepfake content created by generative adversarial network (GAN) models. Deepfakes, which include altered audio and/or video clips that are nearly identical to real ones, can be used maliciously for things like propaganda, cybercrimes, and political campaigns. To address this challenge, a comparison is conducted involving several CNN models, like EfficientNetB0, VGG-16, DenseNet121, VGG-19, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, InceptionV3, and Xception for deepfake detection. The models are trained using transfer learning technique and by fine-tuning them on the dataset using various hyperparameters. The performance analysis was performed on six cases in which the optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and epochs were adjusted. By exploring this comparative study, a contribution is made to the development of more robust solutions for detecting deepfakes. A thorough analysis of different pre-trained models is conducted and verified, based on the reported outcomes, ResNet50 outperforms the other models. The evaluation of the model's performance involves the comparison of various metrics that have been identified, such as Accuracy, Precision, AUC-ROC curve, and F1-score.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Stroke Risk Assessment Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Brain stroke is a major health concern since it is the second leading cause of death and the third leading cause of disability worldwide. Early identification and prevention of stroke are crucial for reducing its consequences on people and healthcare systems. In this study, we provide a predictive modeling approach for assessing the risk of stroke based on machine learning algorithms. We examine and compare the efficacy of several models using a large dataset that includes a range of patient attributes. Our research includes data exploration, preprocessing, model creation, and performance evaluation. According to the data, the selected model, logistic regression, achieved an impressive maximum accuracy of 94.6%. The accuracy rates are promising. We also discuss how the interpretability of these models impacts clinical decision-making. This study reduces the load on healthcare systems and improves patient outcomes by using machine learning methods. Additionally, it emphasizes how sophisticated analytics may help medical professionals implement early intervention techniques, which is a development that is beneficial for continuous attempts to avoid stroke.

articleTitle: 16-bit Vedic multiplier Using Carry Skip Adder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Inspired by the effective calculation techniques found in ancient Indian Vedic mathematics., this project implements a 16-bit Vedic multiplier. The main goal is to enhance the Vedic multiplier performance by integrating it with a Carry Skip Adder (CSKA)., which is renowned for its ability to expedite binary addition by skipping over blocks that do not require carry-in processing. This integration aims to leverage the CSKA's potential to reduce carry propagation time significantly., thus optimizing the overall multiplication process. A Carry Select Adder (CSA)., which computes the sum and carry values for both possible inputs beforehand., is compared. This comparison focuses on evaluating the two systems' performance based on critical metrics such as computational speed., silicon area requirement., and power consumption. Through systematic design., simulation., and analysis using tools like VHDL/Verilog and Xilinx or ModelSim for circuit implementation., and Cadence or Synopsys for performance estimation., this project aims to ascertain the most efficient combination of Vedic multiplication technique with advanced adder designs. This research is expected to provide important new information about improving digital multiplication techniques. It promotes the integration of mathematical concepts from antiquity with modern digital electronics to improve speed., minimize area usage., and lower power consumption.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Algorithms for Robust Cyber Threat Detection and Classification: A Comprehensive Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: In response to the escalating frequency and complexity of cyber threats, the imperative need to enhance cybersecurity measures is evident. This study explores the potential of machine learning (ML) algorithms in advancing threat detection and classification by automating the identification of security incidents. The abstract presents a thorough assessment of various ML algorithms, including decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks, for their efficacy in detecting and categorizing cyber threats. The evaluation encompasses a diverse dataset featuring different cyber-attack scenarios and incorporates multiple features such as network traffic patterns, system logs, and user behavior. Performance metrics, such as training accuracy and testing accuracy, are employed to assess the effectiveness of each algorithm. Furthermore, the study investigates the impact of feature selection techniques and model optimization strategies on algorithm performance. The results underscore the capability of ML algorithms to accurately identify and categorize cyber threats, providing valuable insights into their strengths and limitations. This research contributes to the field of cybersecurity by facilitating the development of practical and robust ML-based solutions, ultimately reinforcing cyber defence mechanisms against evolving threats.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Parkinson's Disease Detection Through Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: One of the biggest issues with worldwide public health is Parkinson's disease (PD). It is usually known that about are around one million Americans who have Parkinson's disease, whereas there are approximately five million cases of the condition globally. As a result, it's critical to identify Parkinson's disease early on and make the appropriate treatment plans. These days, machine learning is essential for analysing problems in real time and offering answers thanks to its widely used algorithms. These days, machine learning algorithms are used in the healthcare industry to identify patients' health problems. This research went into great detail about the methods used using algorithms that use machine learning to classify Parkinson's disease. A fault in the brain cells that generate dopamine, a necessary chemical for synapses to connect with one another, is the cause of Parkinson's disease. The brain's dopamine-producing neurons are in charge of control, flexibility, and event familiarity. When 60–80% of these cells disappear, inadequate dopamine is produced, which causes Parkinson's disease symptoms to manifest. In this case, the Random Forest, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbours, and Support Vector Machine techniques were used to identify the illness. Compared to Decision Tree and Support Vector Machine, Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbours offer the best performance.

articleTitle: Advancing Trust in the Internet: Blockchain-driven Decentralized VPNs Leveraging Smart Contracts and PoS as Trust Factor Calculators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The imperative need for a secure and privacy-focused virtual private network (VPN) solution arises amidst growing concerns about centralized VPN architectures. The limitations of existing VPN models are examined, emphasizing issues related to single points of control, susceptibility to attacks, and potential privacy breaches. To counter these challenges, a decentralized VPN system built upon the blockchain client that supports smart contracts and proof of stake (PoS) is proposed. The blockchain-based architecture is designed to enhance security, transparency, and accountability in VPN operations. By leveraging distributed ledger technology, the proposed system eliminates the risks related to centralized control, offering a more resilient and tamper-resistant infrastructure. Smart contracts and PoS further contribute to the autonomous and trustworthy nature of the decentralized VPN. This contribution aims to advance the current discourse on VPNs by presenting a solution that addresses the shortcomings of traditional models.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Experimental Possibilities of a Logical Wireless Power Transfer System Design for Charging Electric Vehicles Through High Intensity Concentration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: An exciting new direction in electric vehicle (EV) energy supply system development is the wireless power transfer (WPT) method. The WPT outshines plug-in hybrid electrical charging systems in many respects, including its compact battery size, low weight, rapid charging capabilities (charging-in-motion services), and extensive range while on the go. After establishing the framework and categorization of the WPT system, this article goes on to examine the fundamentals of the most well-known WPT method, electromechanical reactive resonance transmission. Through the use of wireless technology, known as wireless power transfer (WPT), electric energy may be sent wirelessly from an energy source to a load. With their numerous benefits over their wired counterparts—including the elimination of exposed cables, simplified charging, and unfaltering transfer of power even in harsh environments—wireless power transceivers (WPTs) are finding widespread usage in industrial settings. Several businesses are considering using WPTs to power the electric vehicle (EV)'s internal batteries, and they're working to enhance and advance the many related topologies. The low-cost inductive connection of two coils, the transmitter and receiver coils, allows for WPT to function. The transmitter coils for electric car charging applications are buried under the road, while the receiver coils are installed inside the vehicle. In this study, a novel approach to power transfer is presented, HIWPT. To assess its efficacy, it is cross-validated with an existing technique, CPTS, which stands for Conventional Power Transfer System. Regarding moderately high transfer of power usage, such as charging electric vehicles, capacitive WPT of the resonance type is typically preferred because to its higher efficiency. While designing the WPT system's power supply stages, we took into account the following factors(i) the values and ratings of the capacitors that render the coil-coupling resonance; (ii) the electricity gadgets of converters that supply the power to the receiving coil, including the rectifier diode as well as the in-cascade chopper, which control the battery feed; and (iii) the electrical components of the prefrontal cortex rectifiers and the ultra-high frequency converter which supply the transmitting coil. We used cutting-edge power electronic gear for a high-frequency converter so that the WPT system could reach its full potential.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Manhole Management System for Real-time Status, Water Level, and Gas Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Regular monitoring of the maintenance manhole system is imperative to uphold the city's health and cleanliness standards. Our study offers an intelligent manhole that monitors the manhole's condition, water level, and gases. We tested the status, gas, and water levels of our revolutionary, innovative manhole in several places. Our system's Blink app position tracking of our smart manhole is critical. This capability improves monitoring efficiency and speeds up issue resolution. Our work revolutionizes municipal utility maintenance and safety by optimizing manhole performance. Integrating a Node MCU, GPS module, gas sensor, ultrasonic sensor, and Android Blynk software creates a complete real-time monitoring and data-collecting system. Combining these technologies, our Manhole Monitoring System improves safety and streamlines maintenance, making municipal infrastructure more robust and efficient. This paper highlights the promising features of IoT and shows how it may be used to improve the smart manhole. In the future, this creative method may result in a more durable and better intelligent city.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Security in Cloud-Based Soil Carbon Sequestration Monitoring Systems Using Random Forest Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The evaluation of the protections of soil carbon sequestration monitoring technique using cloud computing and machine learning. The implementation of these systems is essential for development of agricultural industry that is friendly to the environment for reducing the effect on the environment. As a consequence of recent developments in technology, including cloud computing, these surveillance systems are now far more effective than they were before. However, the storing of data on the cloud creates worries over the security of the data. Using Random Forest Regression (RFR) it potential these difficulties. Through the use of this method, the potential to improve the safety of data collection is utilized. With the examination of patterns within the data that has been collected to identify possible security. The capabilities of ensemble learning are responsible for the improved consistency and precision with which it operates. According to the findings of the studies, this method makes the process of collecting and analyzing data on soil carbon more secure. For maintaining confidentiality this is beneficial for both environmentally responsible farming and sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Pest Detection and Prevention for Agricultural Crops Using YoloV8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Agriculture's productivity depends on seasonal rains, weather, and pesticides. Due to a lack of knowledge about pests, farmers are unable to take preventive measures within the stipulated time, resulting in decreased crop productivity. Here, pest detection is very helpful in increasing food quality and also helps the country's economy. This paper describes the development of a deep learning-based agricultural insect detection system. A web-based application and an algorithm for vermin detection comprise the system. The YOLOV8 architecture uses convolutional neural networks (CNN), bottlenecks, convolution to flatten (C2F), and detection blocks for feature extraction, representation learning, and pest detection. Finally, the system was implemented in Python in the Visual Studio 2022 environment, and a web application was developed using the Streamlit library. The system detects the uploaded pest images, and identifies the diseases, and suggests remedies on the web application. The system constructed to detect 10 kinds of agricultural pests inhabiting the crops, such as citrus, paddy, cotton, mango, tomato, lady's finger, and pomegranate. The findings demonstrate 95%% efficacy. It is better than Resnet50,EfficientDet and Yolo's previous versions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Since diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the primary cause of blindness in working-age adults worldwide, vision loss must be avoided by receiving early detection and treatment. In recent years, deep learning techniques have become more and more useful tools for automated drug discovery, possibly offering solutions to overcome the limitations of traditional screening methods. In-depth descriptions of the most recent deep learning methods for DR detection are provided in this review article. We begin by discussing the importance of DR screening, its prevalence, and the challenges faced by healthcare systems in managing this condition. Next, we discuss different deep learning architectures used for DR detection, such as CNNs and RNNs, and their combinations. We investigate how to improve the precision, resilience, and interpretability of DR detection models through the use of explainable AI, ensemble methods, transfer learning, and attention mechanisms. We also examine publicly available datasets, evaluation metrics, and preprocessing techniques that are commonly used to benchmark DR detection algorithms. We discuss the limitations and possible uses of deep learning-based deep readout detection, emphasizing the significance of large-scale, diverse datasets, the interpretability of the model, and real-world deployment concerns. The overall objectives of this review are to advance the field of automated DR detection by highlighting recent developments, compiling existing knowledge, and identifying areas that require further research.

articleTitle: Multimodal machine learning approach for detecting spyware and ransomware
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: This study acquaints one with an encyclopaedic approach of the machine learning field which is distinctively designed for the identification of the risk imported by the two trenchant and widespread malwares, spyware and ransomware. With spyware and ransomware posing substantial threats to both individuals and businesses worldwide, recent reports underscore the urgency to solve these problems on an urgent basis. Check Point Research's findings reveal a 55.5% surge in attempted ransomware attacks compared to the previous year, locking the target over 1 in 10 organizations globally. Additionally, the Positive Technologies report for Q3 2023 highlights a 65% increase in spyware attacks on individuals compared to the prior quarter. This underscores the critical need for robust detection mechanisms. Our study aims to address this challenge by exploring multiple innovative approaches to malware detection. In our research, we found that Support Vector Machine (SVM) and XGBoost demonstrate the best performance, with accuracies of 99.7% and 99.6% respectively. We seek to further improve cybersecurity practices in the digital age by showcasing the scalability and efficacy of our suggested strategy in practical settings through experimental evaluation and analysis.

articleTitle: Handwritten Signature Recognition using MobileCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Classifying handwritten signatures becomes important when it comes to document verification. In order to maximize the precision and effectiveness of the signature examination process, this research presents a robust method for classifying handwritten signatures that makes use of Convolutional Neural Networks, and the light-weight Mobile Net architecture. Because of the inherent differences and quirks in each person's handwriting style, classifying signatures is a difficult operation that requires a method that can recognize and learn these subtle differences. By integrating a CNN, the suggested model MobileCNN successfully extracts hierarchical characteristics from the signature photos. The Mobile Net design also guarantees the model's portability and adaptability to a range of devices, including ones with little processing power. Additionally, our method makes use of transfer learning and data augmentation techniques to improve the model's performance and generalization skills on unseen data. According to experimental findings, the suggested signature classification system exhibits impressive accuracy and low latency, which qualifies it as a viable option for real-time use in the domains of identity authentication and secure document verification.

articleTitle: Leveraging ML Power for Crowdfunding Success Evaluation and Security Enforcement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Numerous online portals have been developed over time, to host large-scale and global crowdfunding campaigns<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> in order to fulfill the funding goals of the listed projects. Therefore it becomes essential to be able to assess the probability of success of these campaigns based on the provided parameters. In this dynamic landscape of Online crowdfunding, ensuring the security<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup> and integrity<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>of such a model to safeguard the interests of the investors is imperative to develop a high degree of credibility of the platform. This research introduces a sophisticated Machine Learning (ML) model<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4]</sup>which is tailored according to a specifically extracted dataset which works upon a comprehensive range of features like number of images, campaign timeline, textual description, security score, associated industry and other related attributes. A distinctive feature of this study includes engineering textual features<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[5]</sup>from the campaign description to analyze its impact on the accuracy of the predictive model. One of the key components of this research initiative lies in discerning the scam or fraudulent campaigns listed upon the platform. The model was evaluated under several metrics to ensure its thoroughness. Notably, the Logistic Regression (LR) model was the best performer, showing a favorable ROC curve and a high accuracy of 0.899, which indicated that our predictive model was successful in its objective. Furthermore, by emphasizing the identification and suspension of fraudulent campaigns, our study fills a significant research gap and safeguards investor interests while promoting platform confidence. Our study increases investor trust in online crowdfunding ecosystems and by offering a strong foundation for well-informed decision-making. Our research offers a novel and thorough method for using machine learning to improve the effectiveness, security, and legitimacy of crowdfunding platforms.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning framework-based intrusion detection system for the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The recent surge in Internet of Things (IoT) devices has brought about unique security challenges. These devices have limited resources and are vulnerable to attacks. As Internet use becomes more widespread, network security has become a top priority, and network intrusion detection has emerged as a crucial technology for protecting systems. However, the original data sources for intrusion detection often have high dimensionality and large volumes, which can impact efficiency and accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (HCRNN-IDS) based intrusion detection system to detect malicious packets in real time. By utilizing a newly developed benchmark Netflow-based dataset like NF-QU-NIDS, our system can efficiently detect twenty different network attacks. We have conducted empirical evaluations to validate the accuracy of our model, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, we have compared our proposed system with state-of-the-art intrusion detection methods, proving that our system achieves a superior accuracy rate of 98.44%.

articleTitle: Breaking Through Color Casts: Enhancing Image Fidelity with Machine Learning-Based Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: L Color cast, an aberration common in digital images, poses challenges in various image processing applications, affecting image quality and visual perception. This research investigates diverse methodologies for color cast correction, ranging from traditional algorithms to modern machine learning-based approaches. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of original and corrected images, the present study evaluates the efficacy of each method using quantitative metrics, including ACMO, BREN, GRAS, LAPM, LAPV, LAPD, and WAVV. Results indicate that while traditional techniques like Gray World Algorithm and White Patch Retinex Algorithm demonstrate moderate effectiveness, the implemented machine learning-based algorithm showcases superior performance across multiple color cast levels. By employing linear regression on RGB values, the method efficiently corrects color cast aberrations, yielding visually appealing and perceptually accurate results. Furthermore, the research highlights the significance of robust color constancy algorithms and their role in mitigating color cast distortions in digital images. This study contributes valuable insights into the field of color cast correction, offering practitioners in image processing and computer vision a comprehensive understanding of effective correction strategies. Future research directions may explore advanced machine learning models and integration with color constancy mechanisms to further enhance color cast correction techniques.

articleTitle: Trading Automation Using PineScript
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: This research project presents a comprehensive initiative that combines the development of an efficient website scraper with an algorithmic trading system. The website scraper, designed to extract diverse data elements such as text, images, links, and product information, aims to empower students and new learners in the field with the ability to access, analyze, and comprehend web data for applications like market research and competitive analysis. The trading system utilizes a indicator based on Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Bollinger Bands for real-time Buy and Short signals in index trading. Parameters and real-time display enhance adaptability and analysis. The initiative includes the integration of a simulator into a financial platform, offering users a realistic experience to understand investment strategies, mitigate risks, and optimize financial performance. The simulator, the real stock market using historical and real-time data, provides a risk-free environment for users to practice investment plans. The approach aims to make internet investing more accessible and informed, bridging the gap between data extraction, analysis, and algorithmic trading for a comprehensive understanding of investment opportunities in a dynamic market environment.

articleTitle: Decentralized Identity and Access Management (IAM) Using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: In this transformative initiative, Identity and Access Management (IAM) undergoes a profound evolution through decentralized blockchain technology. The project focuses on developing a user-centric identity wallet, leveraging blockchain's attributes for transparency, immutability, and cryptographic security, orchestrating smart contracts to automate identity verification and access control. This decentralized IAM architecture not only fortifies security but also empowers users with ownership and sovereignty over their personal data, ensuring a tamper-resistant environment and fostering a more resilient and user-centric digital landscape. The project's strategic alignment with interoperability standards amplifies its impact, promising to set new benchmarks for secure and efficient IAM frameworks across industries.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Oriented Human Body Enabled Communication Protocol Design for Health Monitoring Services
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has transformed healthcare by enabling remote patient monitoring, chronic disease management, and preventive care solutions. Human Body Communication (HBC) stands out as a promising integration within this evolution, utilizing the body's electrical conductivity for seamless data transmission between wearable health devices and healthcare systems. This direct connection ensures secure, real-time monitoring without traditional connectivity constraints. Proposing a protocol design framework, this abstract aims to optimize communication between IoT and HBC technologies to enhance health monitoring services and the framework accommodates a variety of sensors crucial for comprehensive health assessment, including temperature, EEG, ECG, heart rate, pressure, blood glucose, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and blood pressure sensors. By integrating IoT and HBC, healthcare enters a new era characterized by improved accessibility, efficiency, and personalized care delivery. This convergence fosters proactive healthcare, empowering individuals to manage their well-being while enabling healthcare providers to deliver timely interventions for better patient outcomes.

articleTitle: System of IntelliGuard Access Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: In this study, the ESP32-CAM module and Internet of Things technologies are integrated into a Smart Door Lock System to present a revolutionary approach to home security. As the visual core, the ESP32-camera takes high-resolution pictures that supply vital visual context for reliable face recognition algorithms. By precisely confirming the identification of people at the entrance, this technique improves security by lowering the possibility of unwanted access. The integration of a bot system enables smooth communication by instantly sharing photos that are taken with users across many channels. By utilizing Internet of Things concepts, the system allows for remote access and monitoring, empowering individuals with photos and notifications in real-time, regardless of their location. The system's adaptability makes it useful not just in home settings but also in commercial and institutional ones. The study emphasizes user privacy and ethical deployment while addressing security and ethical issues related to facial recognition technology. Finally, our study represents a major breakthrough in smart home security by providing improved access control as well as a new definition of user participation and monitoring through the use of cutting-edge technology tomer loyalty in the evolving e-commerce landscape.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an IoT based Intelligent Energy Meter using Less Expensive Controller Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: With an eye towards improving the efficacy of energy monitoring and management, this research offers a thorough approach for the creation of an Intelligent Energy Metre that is based on the Internet of Things. A key component of the system is the use of specialized sensors to continuously measure electrical characteristics like voltage and current. These sensors generate analog signals, which are conditioned, digitized, and processed by a microcontroller. Algorithms within the firmware/software calculate energy consumption metrics, which are transmitted wirelessly to a central server or cloud platform using secure communication protocols. The collected data is then stored and analyzed to provide insights into energy usage patterns, facilitating informed decision-making for optimizing energy efficiency and reducing costs. The methodology encompasses various stages, including market research, hardware and software development, integration, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Through the implementation of this methodology, a robust and scalable IoT-based energy monitoring system can be developed, empowering users to make informed decisions for sustainable energy management.

articleTitle: Stacking Framework for Detecting Braktooth Attack on IoT Health Care Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The rise in Internet of Things (IoT) devices, particularly in healthcare systems, has brought about significant security concerns, especially with the widespread use of Bluetooth technology. The discovery of BrakTooth vulnerabilities in the Bluetooth Classic (BT Classic) stack further amplifies these risks, potentially compromising sensitive medical data and patient safety. In light of this, the present study proposes a unique framework for detecting BrakTooth attacks on IoT healthcare systems. By utilizing the stacking ensemble algorithm and the ISOT BrakTooth dataset, the framework aims to identify anomalies related to BrakTooth in Bluetooth traffic at the Link Manager Protocol (LMP) layer. The framework's effectiveness is demonstrated through extensive experimentation, achieving an accuracy rate of 94.01%. The results highlight the system's capability to proactively detect and mitigate BrakTooth vulnerabilities, bolstering cybersecurity resilience in interconnected healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of an Elliptical Curve Cryptographic Model Based Data Security Over Communication Channels Using Cybersecurity Logics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: In light of the escalating cybersecurity challenges, we propose a comprehensive approach to evaluating the effectiveness of an Elliptic Curve Cryptographic (ECC) model in enhancing data security over communication channels. Our hybrid model integrates ECC with advanced cybersecurity logics to provide multi-layered defense against cyber threats. The methodology involves several key steps. Firstly, optimal ECC parameters are selected through a hybrid approach that combines genetic algorithms and statistical analysis, ensuring robustness and efficiency in parameter selection. Subsequently, secure keys are generated using ECC-specific algorithms and random number generation techniques, guaranteeing the confidentiality and integrity of cryptographic keys. Lastly, a hybrid encryption process is implemented, combining ECC with symmetric key cryptography to optimize efficiency while maintaining high levels of security. Through this comprehensive approach, we aim to provide a thorough evaluation of the ECC model's effectiveness in securing communication channels against a variety of cyber threats.

articleTitle: Segmentation Method of Deterministic Feature Extraction for Identification of Brain Tumor Using MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Segmentation of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning. This paper presents a segmentation method utilizing deterministic feature clustering for the accurate identification of brain tumors from MRI images. The proposed method integrates feature extraction techniques to capture relevant characteristics of tumor regions, followed by a deterministic clustering algorithm to partition the extracted features into distinct classes corresponding to tumor and non-tumor regions. The feature clustering process incorporates spatial constraints to enhance segmentation accuracy and mitigate noise sensitivity. Experimental evaluations on diverse MRI datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately delineating tumor boundaries and differentiating tumor regions from healthy brain tissue. Comparative analyses against state-of-the-art segmentation methods underscore the superiority of the proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. The proposed segmentation method holds significant promise for improving the precision and reliability of brain tumor identification in clinical practice, thereby facilitating more effective treatment planning and patient care.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Government Fund Disbursal System using Blockchain and IPFS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: In the modern landscape, most governments have financial incentives linked to most activities such as education in the form of scholarships, production and manufacturing in the form of production linked incentives (PLIs) and social security and retirement benefits. These social benefits sometimes take the form of giving financial assistance directly to the eligible in the form of bank transfers. However, these schemes are generally opaque in their operation in terms of allocation and timely disbursement of funds, leading to distrust in the government. This lack of transparency and inefficiency is generally attributed to corruption in local governmental bodies. Hence, a solution is required which introduces trackable and auditable disbursal of funds. Blockchain has been proposed as a viable solution for this purpose as fundamentally each transaction is recorded on a public ledger. However, multiple options exist for decentralized file storage such as Filecoin and Arweave, but they have built in incentives for pooling storage, leading to higher costs. And hence, the proposed model uses blockchain to execute smart contracts to establish the eligibility of an applicant, stores the applicant's necessary documents using the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) protocol, and transfers the funds in a decentralized manner.

articleTitle: Enhancing Machine Learning Model Accuracy through Novel SDNIoT Dataset Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: Cyberattacks in SDN environments pose grave threats, exploiting vulnerabilities in software-defined networks. These attacks jeopardize data integrity, network security, and overall system stability, necessitating robust defense measures and vigilant monitoring. Here we present a novel method for building a customized dataset for this machine learning project, with an emphasis on understanding how the attacks differ in nature when compared with legitimate requests and research purpose against compared Internet of Things (IoT) vulnerabilities and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) assaults. Recognizing that good training data is essential, we describe in detail the dataset construction procedure, including data collection, anno-tation, and synthesis. In the data collecting stage, we investigate in detail how to acquire representative and varied samples, locate important data sources, and extract pertinent data. An important component of dataset enrichment is annotation, which entails meticulous processes for classifying and labeling data with professional advice to promote pattern identification. Further-more, synthesis is essential because it complements the dataset with artificial data that replicates real-world events, diversifies the inputs, and increases the adaptability of the DT algorithm. We describe in fully the methods used to generate synthetic data, highlighting their importance in strengthening the model's resistance to fluctuations and outliers. The suggested approach attempts to train DT algorithms capable of efficiently detecting and mitigating security risks in complex network environments by incorporating IoT device behaviors and DDoS attack patterns into the dataset.

articleTitle: Strategic Mobility Insights: Optimizing Parking and Operational Efficiency through Density Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: This research introduces a comprehensive approach to optimize parking and operational efficiency by employing density analysis based on entrance and exit camera footage in public spaces, such as malls or educational institutions. The study focuses on vehicle tracking to estimate crowd density within these locations, utilizing image processing techniques to count the number of vehicles entering and exiting the public space. The computed crowd density serves as a pivotal metric for proactive alert systems that trigger interventions when congestion levels are critical, redirecting incoming traffic to alternative parking areas. In addition to real-time density management, the research explores trends in crowd density variations across different days, offering insights for strategic resource planning and operational adjustments. The implemented alert system demonstrates its effectiveness in managing high-density situations, providing a dynamic solution for optimizing parking resources and overall crowd-related resources. This research contributes to the evolution of intelligent urban management systems by presenting a robust methodology that integrates both parking management and crowd density trends, setting the stage for future innovations in resource optimization.

articleTitle: A Robust Data Security Model Development to Maintain the Integrity of Information Using Artificial Intelligence and Cyber Laws
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity (ISCS)
abstract: The field of artificial intelligence (AI) has seen significant advancements in recent years. These days, artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being utilized by organizations in both the public and commercial sectors all over the world. Individuals, organizations, and society as a whole will reap broad and significant advantages as a result of the capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) both today and in the near future. Nevertheless, these very same technical advancements give rise to significant concerns, such as the question of how to ensure that artificial intelligence technology is built and implemented in a manner that is in accordance with the applicable data privacy laws and standards. The fast development of artificial intelligence presents substantial hurdles in terms of protecting customers' privacy and the confidentiality of their data. The purpose of this essay is to suggest an all-encompassing strategy for the development of a framework to solve these concerns. First, an overview of prior research on security and privacy in artificial intelligence is presented, with an emphasis on both the progress that has been made and the limits that still remain. In the same vein, open research topics and gaps that need to be addressed in order to improve existing frameworks are recognized. Regarding the development of the framework, the topic of data protection in artificial intelligence is discussed.
